conceptName: Configuring garbage collection and orphan-mapping behavior

items.stem: What does GarbageCollectionBehavior control, and what is its default?

options.text: Which unreferenced destination entities garbage collection deletes; it defaults to DeleteCreated (only ones this system instance created)
How many exceptions abort a segment; it defaults to 30
Whether orphan mappings are removed; it defaults to Remove
The order of Migration and GarbageCollection segments in a Run

items.explanation: GarbageCollectionBehavior bounds which unreferenced destination entities GC removes; the conservative default is DeleteCreated (only entities this system created).

misconceptions.c: That's OrphanMappingBehavior (default None) — a separate knob about mappings, not destination-entity deletion scope.

items.stem: Which GarbageCollectionBehavior is the most aggressive — deleting even unreferenced destination records this sync never created?
items.explanation: DeleteCreated (default) removes only what this system created; DeleteMapped adds anything with a mapping; DeleteAll removes every unreferenced entity, even pre-existing ones. Use DeleteAll only when the sync owns the whole set.

misconceptions.b: DeleteCreated is the safest/most conservative — only entities this system created.
misconceptions.d: None isn't a GarbageCollectionBehavior value; it's an OrphanMappingBehavior value.

items.stem: OrphanMappingBehavior governs what happens to a mapping whose source entity has disappeared. What are its options and default?

options.text: None (default; leave the mapping active), Deactivate, or Remove
It always removes the mapping; there is no choice

items.explanation: OrphanMappingBehavior is None (default — mapping stays active), Deactivate (deactivated but kept), or Remove (removed entirely).

misconceptions.b: Those are GarbageCollectionBehavior values (destination deletion scope), not orphan-mapping disposition.
misconceptions.d: The default is actually None — nothing is removed unless you opt in.

items.stem: An entity's OrphanMappingBehavior is left at None. What does that mean for the orphan-mapping abort threshold (L1.12)?

options.text: There's nothing for it to act on — with None, orphan mappings stay active and are never identified for removal, so that threshold doesn't apply; GarbageCollectionBehavior is the cleanup lever instead
The threshold fires immediately on every run
None forces all mappings to be removed

items.explanation: None means no orphan processing, so no mappings are identified for deactivation/removal and the orphan threshold has nothing to evaluate. Deactivate/Remove are what create orphan candidates (and, with Remove, the L3.4 dedup-recovery path on re-run).

misconceptions.c: None is the opposite — it leaves mappings active.
misconceptions.d: Orphan behavior governs mappings, not whether garbage collection runs.

items.source: lessons/L2.8.md - orphan behavior None and the L1.12 threshold

items.stem: You sync SharePoint asset permissions and the sync is the authoritative owner of that permission set: any permission in the destination the source no longer lists should be removed — even ones some earlier process created. The external system's default is DeleteMapped. What GarbageCollectionBehavior do you set, where, and why?
rubric: Set GarbageCollectionBehavior = DeleteAll — delete every unreferenced destination entity, not just those this system created or mapped
Set it on the [EntityType] for that permission entity (a per-entity override), so it applies to just that entity
The more specific [EntityType] setting overrides the broader [ExternalSystem] default (DeleteMapped)
Rationale: the sync is authoritative for the full set, so aggressive cleanup is correct here despite being riskier than the default DeleteCreated
items.sampleAnswer: Set GarbageCollectionBehavior = DeleteAll on the [EntityType] for the permission entity. DeleteAll removes every unreferenced destination record, including ones this sync didn't create — appropriate because the sync owns the entire permission set, so anything the source no longer lists shouldn't remain. Because a per-entity-type setting overrides the system-wide default, this entity uses DeleteAll while the rest of the SchoolObjectModel/SharePoint system stays on its DeleteMapped default. It's the aggressive end of the scale, justified only by the sync being authoritative here.
